critic_scores.rationale: The single example given ('barnet'/'ett barn') is factually correct, but the response critically omits that Swedish has two grammatical genders — common (utrum) and neuter (neutrum) — which determine whether the indefinite article is 'en' or 'ett' and whether the definite suffix is '-en' or '-et'. Without this, the response is misleading by implying only one pattern exists. The previously flagged issue FC-001 about grammatical gender and definite suffix differences remains entirely unaddressed.
